# Taste design, optional visual lens

Choose one coherent direction appropriate to the actual users and task. Use this as an optional creative lens, never as global rules that override an existing design system, accessibility or source parity. This is a text adaptation, not the upstream experimental runtime or full skill collection.

1. Inspect current screens, brand/type/color tokens, task density and approved UI behavior before proposing changes.
2. Present a restrained option and, only when useful, one bolder option. Explain concrete trade-offs in readability, hierarchy, density and implementation cost.
3. Use deliberate spacing, clear type hierarchy, consistent alignment and meaningful emphasis. Reuse existing fonts/components/icons; do not impose upstream font bans, bento layouts, fixed colors or mandatory animation.
4. Use real approved content or visibly labeled examples. Do not invent testimonials, customer names, metrics or compliance claims. Never pull remote images/fonts without authorization and a need.
5. Cover keyboard/focus, contrast, responsive/zoom behavior, reduced motion and all error/loading/empty states. A quiet business tool may benefit from little or no motion.
6. Produce a reviewable visual/specification first. Implement only the authorized design slice, with source-rule links, segment review and measured/observed checks.

No new framework, icon/font library, animation package or backend is required by this adaptation. Upstream minimalist/redesign directions are optional references, not mandatory code prescriptions. See SOURCE.md and LICENSE.
